from.place: The sentence: ‘The fixed-base property does not imply the universal one: there are flat, finitely presented f with geometrically connected fibres for which BC(f,n,0) holds but BC(f_{\mathbf A^1_S},n,0) fails, so the quantifier over S'\to S cannot be dropped from the hypotheses.’

title: Fixed-base base change need not be universal
statement: There exist a base scheme $S$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], an integer $n\geq1$ invertible on $S$, and a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphism $f:X\to S$ with geometrically connected fibres [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois] such that $BC(f,n,0)$ holds at the fixed base, while $BC(f_{\mathbf A^1_S},n,0)$ fails after base change along the affine-line projection $\mathbf A^1_S\to S$. Here $BC$ is the predicate of [sbc-def-base-change-property], $f_{\mathbf A^1_S}:X\times_S\mathbf A^1_S\to\mathbf A^1_S$ is its base change [sbc-def-base-change-square], and $\mathbf A^1_S$ denotes the scheme obtained by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}(A[t])$ over the affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ of $S$, with its canonical projection to $S$. Thus fixed-base degree-zero base change does not imply the corresponding universal base-change property.
